verdicts.summary: The note's own failure mode (no code fallback link until a call succeeds) is finding 0. I found no other break on the hosted approve path.

The server only checks that the agent's host equals the tunnel hostname. The hosted page then calls whatever address the relay returns. If that address has a different host, approval fails or the agent rejects the result. I cannot read how the relay picks the endpoint.
verdicts.missing: How the relay's connectEnvironment chooses the endpoint (cloudflare_tunnel, t3_relay or manual) for a linked environment. Specifically, whether httpBaseUrl always has the same host as state.tunnelHostname. That code is not in the checkout.
verdicts.scenario: The agent starts on https://T/ and the server redirects to the hosted page. The hosted call goes to authorized.httpBaseUrl, say https://x.t3coderelay.com. requestUrls (McpOAuth.ts:71-76) then sets issuer and resource from that host. sameResource (McpOAuth.ts:397) rejects the agent's resource=https://T/mcp with invalid_target, and approve() would put iss=<relay host> in the redirect (McpOAuth.ts:488-492). Nothing in ApproveAgentSurface checks that the call host matches the agent's host.

verdicts.summary: The 10s bound covers the whole request loop. The first authorizeDpopHttp is outside it but capped at 30s by the renewal fiber's own timeout. A slow renewal fails the request at 10s while the renewal continues and is reused later. The worst-case spinner is roughly 40s, as the note says.

The client rule accepts https, or http on a loopback host. The server's registration rule is the same or narrower, so no registered redirect is blocked. A javascript: or data: URL is refused. Both the load and the decision redirects go through followRedirect.

Approve is gated by canApprove, which includes armed, on both the button and the Enter-submit path. Deny stays enabled. The timer and listeners are cleaned up on unmount. A failed decision does not reset armed.

The note's failure mode (no code from the wizard when the server falls back to its own page) is finding 7. Its open question, whether the remoteClients policy is bypassed, is answered: it is not. The hosted redirect needs a linked Connect tunnel. A policy without remote clients also disallows Connect and revokes cloud-connect sessions, so a Connect session cannot approve.

The note says a decision failure leaves the form usable for retry. That is false when the failure is a CSRF/session mismatch. I confirmed that each token renewal does a new bootstrap exchange that issues a new session id, which answers finding 2's open question. The retry then resends the stale csrfToken and is refused every time until the page is reloaded.

A server release that predates this change still sends users to the hosted /approve-agent page with the old parameters (environment, access, nonce, return_to). The new hosted page cannot handle them, so that handoff dead-ends with 'This sign-in cannot continue'.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A user runs an older server release linked to T3 Connect and opens the agent sign-in on the tunnel host. 2) Its own page shows 'Continue with T3 Connect' (the old continueWithConnect, which built the URL with approveAgentUrl), so the user is sent to app.t3.codes/approve-agent?environment=…&access=…&nonce=…&return_to=…. 3) After this commit deploys, that page is ApproveAgentSurface. environmentId is non-null, but readAuthorizationRequest returns {} because every field is optional and the old params are ignored. 4) The page calls approval with an empty request. The old server fails validateAuthorization with 'names an unknown app', and the page shows 'This sign-in cannot continue'. 5) The code fallback link is not shown, because environment is only set after a successful call. The old hosted page minted the approval code and returned it to the environment; the new page cannot do that.
verdicts.consequence: Every user on an older server who uses the hosted handoff loses it as soon as the hosted app deploys. They must go back to the environment's own page and paste a code, or update the server. The wizard only handles skew in the other direction, through the mcpHostedApproval capability.
